assessment_membership.source: C3-d authoring declaration (2026-09-27): this target is placed in the V1 placement bank's hedging-formula set by this cut's authoring review. The declaration is made here — no authoring fixture and no external assessment export in this repository places this target, so the membership is this review's own and is recorded as such.

texts.text: A hedge that presents a claim as true from one angle only -- the speaker stands partly behind it, and the words mark the part that does not hold.

The phrase stands at the front of the sentence, set off by a comma: In a way, the extra traffic taught us patience. It can also stand inside the clause before the verb (I in a way prefer the quieter office), though the fronted position is the usual one. The words are fixed -- in + a + way, with the article -- and the limited claim follows as a full clause. In speech the comma is the speaker showing one hand: this holds from one side, not from every side.

The article and the preposition are the two slips: the frame is in a way (the article a is part of the stored form, and on does not replace in). The hedge grants the claim only part of its force, so what follows is a claim the speaker is prepared to defend only from one angle; teaching it as plain agreement would be wrong. When a way is a literal route or method (cook it in a way that keeps the grains whole), the hedge is gone.

In a way marks the speaker's own claim as partly true; in some ways counts the angles and needs a plural to follow; sort of and kind of lower the claim with a more colloquial voice. In the way (blocking a path) and in a way that + clause (a manner) are literal readings and are never this hedge.
从某种角度说／在某种程度上（只承认自己说法的一面成立，不是全部）

pedagogical_profile.rationale: Bands are the C3-d authoring judgement (V1 carries no calibration data): the phrase is common in conversation, so receptive value and naturalness are HIGH; core utility and productive value are MEDIUM because the partial-agreement move it makes is subtler than the plain hedges -- it is the right tool when the speaker wants to grant a claim only one angle, and the plainer sort of covers the casual cases. Productive difficulty is MEDIUM: the fixed article and the choice of what follows are what production has to get right. Transfer value is MEDIUM: the angle-marking move transfers to in some ways and to a certain extent. RESOURCE_PRACTICE follows the entity's own declared learning_intent ESTABLISH. Revisit when Calibration100 response data exists.

pack_overlays.rationale: The phrase belongs to the general fluency pack (high-frequency multi-word units), so it carries high weight in that pack's coverage accounting; the shortfall records that it is the partial-agreement member of the hedge family.

Granting a claim one angle before the team weighs it (in a way, the extra traffic taught us patience) is ordinary workplace language, so the unit has a real workplace use; the reduced weight records that the pack's own review has not placed it.

example_policy.policy: Present at most two examples per attempt, whole sentences only: the canonical sentence first; a SUPPORTING or CONTRAST sentence only after the learner has attempted the canonical form twice without producing it. Always show the phrase whole, with the article a and in front, before the comma and the limited claim, and never present a dropped-article, wrong-preposition or literal-manner sentence as a model of the hedge.

typical_errors.error_pattern: In way, + clause (the article a dropped from the fixed frame)
typical_errors.explanation: The frame stores the article -- in a way -- and learners cut it because their own language marks the phrase without one; in way standing alone is not a stored English form.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when the hedged claim is fronted by in way with no article.

typical_errors.error_pattern: On a way, + clause (on standing where the preposition in belongs)
typical_errors.explanation: The frame locates the claim inside one of several angles -- in a way -- and learners swap in on because their own language marks the manner or side with an on-like word; on a way as a hedge is not a stored English form.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when the hedged claim is fronted by on a way.

detection_policy.policy: Fires only on the learner's own produced English text, and only on a visible surface form: the words of the frame at the front of a hedged claim. No model judgement and no confidence score participates (PRODUCT_CONTRACT §8.1: V1 does not treat a model's self-reported high confidence as an R4 certification). The two match rules below state the broken forms the frame's errors take; the do-not-match rules state the accepted realizations and the literal manner reading the hedge must not be read into. The POSITIVE_ERROR fixtures instantiate the two error_patterns; the FALSE_POSITIVE_BOUNDARY fixture states the literal manner reading.

detection_rules.rule: ARTICLE_DROP: match when the hedged claim is fronted by in way with no article, because the frame stores the article (in a way).
PREPOSITION_SLIP: match when the hedged claim is fronted by on a way, because the frame's preposition is in.

ACCEPTED_REALIZATIONS: do not match when the phrase stands whole before its comma (In a way, the extra traffic taught us patience; In a way, I prefer the quieter office.): those are the accepted realizations.

THE_LITERAL_MANNER: do not match when a way is a route or a method of doing something (Cook the rice in a way that keeps the grains whole.), because there the words are a literal manner phrase and the hedging of a claim is not in use.

detection_fixtures.text: In a way, the extra traffic taught us patience.
In a way, I prefer the quieter office.
In a way, her leaving made the team stronger.
Cook the rice in a way that keeps the grains whole.
In way, the extra traffic taught us patience.
On a way, the extra traffic taught us patience.
